```{r}
library(tidyverse)

library(ggplot2)
dfeth <- readRDS("C:/Users/490A/Nextcloud/Research/leg4dev/data/est/dfeth.rds")
dfmlwfull <- readRDS("C:/Users/490A/Nextcloud/Research/leg4dev/data/est/dfmlwfull.rds")
```

# Data used 
```{r}
survey_data <- tribble(
  ~Country,      ~Wave, ~StartYear, ~EndYear,
  "Ethiopia",    "Wave 4", 2018, 2018,
  "Ethiopia",    "Wave 5", 2021, 2021,
  "Malawi",      "Wave 1", 2010, 2010,
  "Malawi",      "Wave 2", 2013, 2013,
  "Malawi",      "Wave 3", 2016, 2016,
  "Malawi",      "Wave 4", 2019, 2019,
  "Tanzania",    "Wave 4", 2014, 2014,
  "Tanzania",    "Wave 5", 2020, 2021
)
ggplot(survey_data, aes(x = StartYear, xend = EndYear, 
                        y = fct_rev(factor(Country)), 
                        yend = fct_rev(factor(Country)))) +
  geom_label(aes(x = StartYear, label = Wave), 
            size = 5, fill="#D4FF1D", color="blue", angle=65) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2010, 2021, by = 1),
                     limits = c(2008, 2022) ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16, color = "blue"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = 45, hjust = 1, color = "blue"))
```


# Ethiopia

## Basic descriptives

There are **`r sum(dfeth$wave=="wave4")`** households in Ethiopian Social Survey (ESS) dataset who have produced maize as a main crop both in ESS4 and ESS5. Among these households, **`r sum(dfeth$rotation == "rotation" & dfeth$wave == "wave4")`** adopted legume rotations in 2017, and **`r sum(dfeth$rotation == "rotation" & dfeth$wave == "wave4" & dfeth$improved_maize == "improved")`** (**`r round(sum(dfeth$rotation == "rotation" & dfeth$wave == "wave4" & dfeth$improved_maize == "improved") / sum(dfeth$rotation == "rotation" & dfeth$wave == "wave4") * 100, 1)`**%) of them have adopted improved maize varieties. In 2020, the number of farmers adopting crop rotation has increased to **`r sum(dfeth$rotation == "rotation" & dfeth$wave == "wave5")`**, and also the number of those adopters who used improved maize seeds have increased to **`r sum(dfeth$rotation == "rotation" & dfeth$wave == "wave5" & dfeth$improved_maize == "improved")`** (**`r round(sum(dfeth$rotation == "rotation" & dfeth$wave == "wave5" & dfeth$improved_maize == "improved") / sum(dfeth$rotation == "rotation" & dfeth$wave == "wave5") * 100, 1)`**%)

::: {style="width:60%; background-color: #E2EFD9 "}
```{r}
dfeth |> 
  count(wave, improved_maize, rotation) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = rotation, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |> 
  kable(
    caption = "Table 1: Legume rotation and improved maize adoption in Ethiopia",
    align = "llcc"
  )
```
:::

# Malawi

## Basic descriptives
In terms of legume rotation, there are obvious differences when comparing Wave 1 and Wave 2 with Wave 3 and Wave 4. This is because of the way the rotation variable was developed in these waves. In wave 1 an 2, we were only able to identify if legume was planted in the dry season following the maize cultivation in the dry season. However, in wave 3 and 4, farmers were asked what crops were planted following the previous rainy season[^1] as well as what crops will be planted after the next rainy season.

::: {.columns} 

::: {.column width="45%; background-color: #E2EFD9;"}
```{r}
dfmlwfull |> 
  count(wave, rotation) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = rotation, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |> 
  kable(
    caption = "Table 2: Differences in legume rotation statistics",
    align = "lcc")
```
:::
::: {.column width="10%"}
:::

::: {.column width="45%; background-color: #E2EFD9;"}
```{r}
dfmlwfull |> 
  count(wave, intercrop) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = intercrop, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |> 
  kable(
    caption = "Table 3: Maize-legume intercropping",
    align = "lcc")
```
:::
